status: YouTube bilingual metadata and 8 public topic playlists synced; timed captions in preparation
scopeNote_zh: 依頻道擁有者授權的YouTube API清單核對58支影片；中英文觀看指引與口述字幕分開整理。
scopeNote_en: 58 videos verified against the channel-owner-authorized YouTube API inventory. Bilingual viewing guides are maintained separately from spoken-word captions.

playlists.description_zh: 以熱身與伸展為主題，觀察活動幅度、節奏與身體感受，為後續太極練習做好準備。
playlists.description_en: Explore comfortable movement, pacing and body awareness during warm-up and stretching, preparing for the tai chi practice that follows.

playlists.description_zh: 從開步預備建立站姿與動作節奏。先觀察腳下支撐、身體方向與起步時機，再依老師指導把動作連起來。
playlists.description_en: Begin with preparation, stance and timing. Observe foot support, body orientation and the opening step, then connect the movement with the instructor’s guidance.

playlists.title_zh: 太極步｜貓步前進與倒退
playlists.title_en: Tai Chi Stepping | Forward and Backward Cat Steps
playlists.description_zh: 把貓步前進與倒退拆成支撐、移重心與落腳，從容觀察腳步的虛實變化。
playlists.description_en: Explore forward and backward cat stepping through support, weight transfer and foot placement, at a pace that makes each transition easier to observe.

playlists.title_en: Second Form | Grasp the Sparrow’s Tail
playlists.description_zh: 以攬鵲尾的掤、捋、擠、按為索引，探索手法、身體轉向與腳下支撐的連續配合。
playlists.description_en: Explore Grasp the Sparrow’s Tail through Ward Off, Roll Back, Press and Push, connecting hand movements, body orientation and support from the feet.

playlists.description_zh: 以輕柔發聲、自然呼吸與下腹覺察為觀察方向，依柯明輝老師的示範體會動作節奏。
playlists.description_en: Explore gentle vocalization, natural breathing and lower-abdominal awareness, following the pace of the instructor’s demonstration.

playlists.description_zh: 觀看武營太極演練，從全身節奏、轉向與動作銜接認識戶外團體練習的樣貌。
playlists.description_en: Explore tai chi practice at Weiwuying through whole-body rhythm, turning and transitions in an outdoor class setting.

playlists.title_zh: 太極拳｜復健與健康觀念
playlists.title_en: Tai Chi | Rehabilitation and Health Concepts
playlists.description_zh: 從復健與健康觀念出發，認識太極練習的目標，整理適合帶回課堂或醫療諮詢的問題。
playlists.description_en: Explore tai chi through rehabilitation and health concepts, and collect useful questions for your instructor or healthcare team.

playlists.title_zh: 課堂複習｜太極步與第一、第二式
playlists.title_en: Class Review | Stepping and Forms One and Two
playlists.description_zh: 重看太極步、開步預備與攬鵲尾，把課堂學過的片段連起來，每次複習選一個新的觀察重點。
playlists.description_en: Revisit stepping, the opening preparation and Grasp the Sparrow’s Tail. Connect familiar class material and choose a fresh observation focus for each replay.

sources.supports: General tai chi background and health research context.

videos.description_zh:
熱身06_修正版
聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

11/19 第5堂課｜慢慢活動身體，觀察舒適幅度，帶著放鬆與專注進入太極練習。

觀看指引：先觀察動作從哪個部位開始、如何帶動身體，再留意放鬆與回到原位的過程。複習時從小幅度開始，讓活動範圍隨身體感受逐漸調整；以老師示範的節奏為觀察參考。

功效目標與原理：熱身是從靜止進入活動的過渡，伸展可作為活動度練習的一部分。把注意力放在肩頸、軀幹與四肢的配合，練習辨認緊繃與舒適的界線，也為後續拳式建立從容的起點。

舒適練習提醒：在淨空地面慢慢練，保持自然呼吸；有疼痛、頭暈或站不穩時先停下休息，個別復健安排請與醫療人員討論。

延伸閱讀：
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/flexibility-exercises/

videos.description_en:
Warm-up and Stretching — Clip 6 (Corrected)
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Class 5, 2026-11-19 | Ease into movement, explore a comfortable range, and bring relaxed attention to your tai chi practice.

Viewing guide: notice where a movement begins and how it carries through the body, then follow the release and return. Begin your own review with a small range and let comfort guide gradual adjustments. Use the instructor’s pace as something to observe and discuss.

Learning goals and principles: warming up provides a transition from stillness into activity. Stretching can form part of mobility practice. Explore the relationship between the shoulders, trunk and limbs, becoming familiar with comfortable movement and a relaxed starting point for the forms that follow.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Further reading:
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/flexibility-exercises/

Grasp the Sparrow’s Tail — Sequences 1–4 — Clip 4 (Corrected)
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Class 5, 2026-11-19 | Use Ward Off, Roll Back, Press and Push as an index for observing coordinated movement.

Viewing guide: observe hand direction, body orientation and foot support separately, then return to the whole movement. Pause at a transition to notice where the weight is and where it moves next. Choose one feature for each replay and give yourself time to explore it.

Learning goals and background: practice coordinating the arms, turning and weight transfer, while developing awareness of the whole sequence. Peng, lu, ji and an are traditional martial-arts terms commonly translated as Ward Off, Roll Back, Press and Push. Use these names as landmarks while following the instructor’s demonstration of the transitions.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Further reading:
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/flexibility-exercises/

videos.description_zh:
熱身07_修正版
聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

11/16 第4堂課｜慢慢活動身體，觀察舒適幅度，帶著放鬆與專注進入太極練習。

觀看指引：先觀察動作從哪個部位開始、如何帶動身體，再留意放鬆與回到原位的過程。複習時從小幅度開始，讓活動範圍隨身體感受逐漸調整；以老師示範的節奏為觀察參考。

功效目標與原理：熱身是從靜止進入活動的過渡，伸展可作為活動度練習的一部分。把注意力放在肩頸、軀幹與四肢的配合，練習辨認緊繃與舒適的界線，也為後續拳式建立從容的起點。

舒適練習提醒：在淨空地面慢慢練，保持自然呼吸；有疼痛、頭暈或站不穩時先停下休息，個別復健安排請與醫療人員討論。

聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

11/16 第4堂課｜慢慢活動身體，觀察舒適幅度，帶著放鬆與專注進入太極練習。

觀看指引：先觀察動作從哪個部位開始、如何帶動身體，再留意放鬆與回到原位的過程。複習時從小幅度開始，讓活動範圍隨身體感受逐漸調整；以老師示範的節奏為觀察參考。

功效目標與原理：熱身是從靜止進入活動的過渡，伸展可作為活動度練習的一部分。把注意力放在肩頸、軀幹與四肢的配合，練習辨認緊繃與舒適的界線，也為後續拳式建立從容的起點。

舒適練習提醒：在淨空地面慢慢練，保持自然呼吸；有疼痛、頭暈或站不穩時先停下休息，個別復健安排請與醫療人員討論。

延伸閱讀：
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/flexibility-exercises/

videos.description_en:
Warm-up and Stretching — Clip 1 (Corrected)
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Class 4, 2026-11-16 | Ease into movement, explore a comfortable range, and bring relaxed attention to your tai chi practice.

Viewing guide: notice where a movement begins and how it carries through the body, then follow the release and return. Begin your own review with a small range and let comfort guide gradual adjustments. Use the instructor’s pace as something to observe and discuss.

Learning goals and principles: warming up provides a transition from stillness into activity. Stretching can form part of mobility practice. Explore the relationship between the shoulders, trunk and limbs, becoming familiar with comfortable movement and a relaxed starting point for the forms that follow.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Further reading:
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/flexibility-exercises/

videos.description_zh:
哼哈二將丹田氣功04_修正版
聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

11/16 第4堂課｜觀察呼吸、發聲與動作的配合，以自然、舒服的方式體會哼與哈。

觀看指引：先觀察老師在何時動作、何時發聲，再注意發聲前後的放鬆。練習時先站穩或坐穩，讓呼吸自然流動；動作與聲音的時機可帶回課堂請老師調整。

文化背景與原理：「哼哈二將」也見於寺廟護法文化；「丹田」在這裡是下腹覺察的傳統口訣。氣功常把姿態、注意力與呼吸相連，這組影片可用來觀察如何在舒適的節奏中協調三者。發聲以輕柔為原則，避免喊叫、憋氣或用力壓腹。

舒適練習提醒：在淨空地面慢慢練，保持自然呼吸；有疼痛、頭暈或站不穩時先停下休息，個別復健安排請與醫療人員討論。

videos.description_en:
Heng–Ha Dantian Qigong — Clip 4 (Corrected)
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Class 4, 2026-11-16 | Observe the relationship between breathing, sound and movement, exploring heng and ha gently and comfortably.

Viewing guide: observe the timing of movement and sound, and the return to a relaxed state. Begin from a steady seated or standing position and let breathing flow naturally. Ask the instructor to help with the coordination of voice and movement.

Cultural background and principles: Heng and Ha are also names associated with temple guardians. Here, dantian is a traditional cue for lower-abdominal awareness. Qigong often links posture, attention and breathing; use these clips to explore that coordination at a comfortable pace. Keep the sound gentle, with relaxed breathing and a soft abdomen.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Further reading:
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/qigong-what-you-need-to-know
https://tcmb.culture.tw/zh-tw/detail?id=140636&indexCode=Culture_Object

Grasp the Sparrow’s Tail — Second Sequence — Clip 3 (Corrected)
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Class 4, 2026-11-16 | Use Ward Off, Roll Back, Press and Push as an index for observing coordinated movement.

Viewing guide: observe hand direction, body orientation and foot support separately, then return to the whole movement. Pause at a transition to notice where the weight is and where it moves next. Choose one feature for each replay and give yourself time to explore it.

Learning goals and background: practice coordinating the arms, turning and weight transfer, while developing awareness of the whole sequence. videos.description_zh:
武營太極拳影片3
聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

認識太極的健康練習目標，找到適合自己的參與方式。

觀看指引：留意介紹的練習目標、參與方式與調整方法。可記下具體問題，例如站姿如何簡化、哪些動作需要扶持、自己適合練多久，再與老師或物理治療師討論。

功效目標與文化背景：太極由中國拳術發展而來，也逐漸成為健康促進與復健領域關注的身心運動。觀看這組介紹時，可把姿態、移動、呼吸與專注四個方向連在一起，思考如何安排持續、適合個人狀況的練習。

舒適練習提醒：在淨空地面慢慢練，保持自然呼吸；有疼痛、頭暈或站不穩時先停下休息，個別復健安排請與醫療人員討論。

videos.description_zh:
太極步(貓步)前進與倒退9
聰動太極拳班｜2026年11月｜柯明輝老師

把前進與倒退拆成支撐、移重心、落腳，慢慢看清楚。

觀看指引：先辨認支撐身體的腳與準備移動的腳，再觀察落腳與移重心的先後。可把步法分成小段重看，對照前進、倒退時的方向變化；自己複習時，從容易控制的小步幅開始。

功效目標與原理：以清楚的支撐與移重心，練習步伐控制、身體位置覺察和動作規劃。中國拳術中的虛實觀念，提供了觀察兩腳分工的語言；把節奏放慢，有助於看清移動過程。

舒適練習提醒：在淨空地面慢慢練，保持自然呼吸；有疼痛、頭暈或站不穩時先停下休息，個別復健安排請與醫療人員討論。

videos.description_en:
Tai Chi Cat Steps — Forward and Backward — Clip 9
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Break forward and backward stepping into support, weight transfer and foot placement.

Viewing guide: identify the supporting foot and the foot preparing to move, then observe the sequence of placement and weight transfer. Replay a short section to compare forward and backward directions. Begin your own review with a manageable step length and follow the instructor’s guidance on spacing and contact.

Learning goals and background: focus on step control, body-position awareness and planning the next movement. The traditional martial-arts idea of substantial and insubstantial offers a way to notice the changing roles of the two legs. A slower pace gives you time to observe the transition.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Further reading:
https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/tai-chi-what-you-need-to-know
https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/exercise/flexibility-exercises/

以掤、捋、擠、按為索引，觀察手、身體與移重心的配合。

Tai Chi Form 2 — Grasp the Sparrow’s Tail (Peng, Lu, Ji, An) — Clip 4
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Use Ward Off, Roll Back, Press and Push as an index for observing coordinated movement.

Viewing guide: observe hand direction, body orientation and foot support separately, then return to the whole movement. Pause at a transition to notice where the weight is and where it moves next. Choose one feature for each replay and give yourself time to explore it.

Learning goals and background: practice coordinating the arms, turning and weight transfer, while developing awareness of the whole sequence. Peng, lu, ji and an are traditional martial-arts terms commonly translated as Ward Off, Roll Back, Press and Push. Use these names as landmarks while following the instructor’s demonstration of the transitions.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Tai Chi Cat Steps — Forward and Backward — Clip 3
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Break forward and backward stepping into support, weight transfer and foot placement.

Viewing guide: identify the supporting foot and the foot preparing to move, then observe the sequence of placement and weight transfer. Learning goals and background: focus on step control, body-position awareness and planning the next movement. The traditional martial-arts idea of substantial and insubstantial offers a way to notice the changing roles of the two legs. A slower pace gives you time to observe the transition.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.

Tai Chi Form 1 — Opening Preparation — Clip 1
SmartAction Tai Chi Class | November 2026 | Instructor: 柯明輝

Observe the preparation and opening step, focusing on steadiness, relaxation and transitions.

Viewing guide: observe the whole-body preparation and the relationship between the feet and the ground. Notice the settled moment before stepping. During review, begin with the stance, then add the arms and explore how the shoulders, elbows and trunk work together in a position you can maintain comfortably.

Learning goals and background: use the preparation to practice posture awareness, attention and a smooth transition into movement. With roots in Chinese martial arts, tai chi connects deliberate action with attentive practice. The opening is an invitation to find your pace before continuing through the form.

Comfortable practice: use a clear floor area, move gently and breathe naturally; pause for pain, dizziness or unsteadiness, and discuss individual rehabilitation plans with your healthcare team.
